title: Multi-View Clustering for Open Knowledge Base Canonicalization

problem.claim: Open knowledge bases contain scattered and redundant facts because noun phrases and relation phrases extracted from text are not canonicalized.

gap.claim: Existing work has leveraged the fact view and context view of knowledge in isolation rather than jointly.

contributions.claim: CMVC is an unsupervised framework that jointly leverages fact and context views to canonicalize open knowledge bases without manually annotated labels.
A multi-view CH K-Means clustering algorithm mutually reinforces view-specific embeddings while accounting for different clustering qualities.
The framework includes an iterative training-data optimization strategy and a Log-Jump algorithm for data-driven prediction of the number of clusters without labels.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors describe CMVC as a novel unsupervised framework that jointly leverages the two knowledge views for open knowledge base canonicalization.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report superiority over state-of-the-art methods in extensive experiments on multiple real-world open knowledge base datasets.

narrative_sequence.summary: OIE methods produce large open knowledge bases, but uncanonicalized phrases create scattered and redundant facts.
Fact and context views provide complementary information, yet prior work has used them separately.
CMVC jointly uses the two views through multi-view clustering, training-data optimization, and label-free cluster-number prediction.
The framework is evaluated against state-of-the-art methods on multiple real-world datasets.
